item.title: Lobsters vs Misago vs FlaskBB in 2026: Lightweight Self-Hosted Forums That Skip the 2 GB Tax
item.description: The standard advice for “I need a forum” is Discourse. The standard outcome is a 2 GB RAM bill, two containers, a Redis instance, and a Sidekiq process — for a community of 400 people discussing bicycle routes. Discourse is excellent software aimed at large communities with paid ops staff. It is also wildly oversized for a club, a product’s user base, an internal Q&A board, or a research group.

item.title: Self-Hosted Traditional Bulletin Board Systems: phpBB vs MyBB vs SMF — Classic Forum Software for 2026
item.description:
Why Self-Host a Traditional Forum?

Before Slack, Discord, and social media groups, online communities were built on bulletin board systems. Platforms like phpBB, MyBB, and Simple Machines Forum (SMF) powered millions of communities — from niche hobby forums to massive technical support boards. Today, these platforms remain actively maintained and offer a compelling alternative to centralized platforms.
